researcher: Codex parallel africa research, integrated by Codex

sources.title: Robin Law: Political Disintegration in the Kingdom of Oyo (1982)
sources.note: Cahiers d’études africaines 22(87), p. 388: imperial extent, cavalry, enslavement, civil war, Ilorin and rebuilding southward.

sources.title: Bournemouth University, African Legacy: Old Oyo, Kosso and Guinea Savannah Sites
sources.note: Brian Hallam palace survey and Kosso wall photographs; interpretation of holes remains explicitly uncertain.

sources.title: Ogundiran and Saunders: Potters’ marks and social relations of ceramic distribution in the Oyo Empire (2011)
sources.note: Authors’ research abstract: excavated cooking and serving bowls at Ede-Ile, early 1600s to 1820s. Azania 46(3), pages 317 to 335. DOI: 10.1080/0067270X.2011.621795.

sources.title: Anthracological analysis of charcoal from Bara, Southwestern Nigeria (2026)
sources.note: Section 4 and Table 3 distinguish Oyo-period contexts ca 1570 to 1835 from much earlier settlement; charcoal indicates fuel choices, not exact recipes.

sources.title: Farouk Ajibade: Clay tobacco pipes in a Yoruba interior, ca 1600 to 1840 (2025)
sources.note: University of Tennessee thesis abstract: Ede-Ile camp-to-town, Atlantic tobacco, pipe similarities, unresolved manufacture.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Oyo-Yoruba Twin Figure, Male (1981.486.1)
sources.note: Object details and curatorial essay: nineteenth-twentieth century, wood/camwood/beads/blueing; care of memorial figures. Not an imperial-period excavation.

sources.title: Samuel Crowther: A Vocabulary of the Yoruba Language (1852)
sources.note: Primary printed dictionary, entry Bu, p. 67: “Bu omi fun mi ki nmo”; English translation. Later Yoruba evidence, not an Old Oyo inscription.

sources.title: Nigeria NCMM: Ancient Kano City Walls and Associated Sites
sources.note: 2007 Nigerian tentative-list submission, Description: wall extensions, gates, Kurmi market and Rumfa’s palace. A nomination account, not UNESCO inscription certification.

sources.title: Kano Archives: Arabic and Ajami manuscripts
sources.note: Abdalla Uba Adamu’s archive; Introduction and catalog entries including Arabic title تاج الدين فيما يجب على الملوك. Copy dates are not all given.

sources.title: West Africa Seen from Moroccan Manuscript Archives (2022)
sources.note: History in Africa, p. 309: al-Maghili’s 1490s visits to Kano/Katsina and advice to Rumfa; manuscript at BNRM.

sources.title: Toyin Falola and Matthew Heaton: A History of Nigeria, chronology
sources.note: Cambridge University Press frontmatter chronology: centralized states 1000 to 1500 and Islamic revolution 1804.

sources.title: Hausaness: language, culture, and identity
sources.note: Publisher’s chapter summary: Hausa identity is historically changing, incorporates diverse backgrounds and intermarriage.

sources.title: Mohammed Bashir Salau: Plantation Slavery in the Sokoto Caliphate, Conclusion
sources.note: 2018 book, pp. 156 to 166, accessible summary: crops, labor arrangements, elites, merchants and 1903 demise.

sources.title: Slavery in Islamic West Africa (2022)
sources.note: Chapter summary: British/French/German conquest, British occupation of Kano 1903 and loss of Sokoto independence.

sources.title: Beverly Mack and Jean Boyd: Nana Asma’u and caliphate women
sources.note: George Mason University primary-source teaching collection, excerpts from One Woman’s Jihad: ch.1 pp. 1 to 2; ch.6 pp. 76 to 91; teaching, elegies and childbirth assistance.

sources.title: Boston University NEH Ajami: Nana Asma’u, Admonition
sources.note: 2022 edited manuscript record: Hausa Ajami, fully vocalized; poem 1855 to 1857, undated Shina Commercial Press reproduction from Northwestern collection.

sources.title: Nana Asma’u, Admonition: English translation
sources.note: 2022 translation, pages 1 to 4: opening, bathing and illness, women’s education and charity; composition dated between 1855 and 1857.

sources.title: Paul Lovejoy: Plantations in the Economy of the Sokoto Caliphate (1978)
sources.note: Journal of African History 19(3), 341 to 368, extract: Bello, textile belt, plantations and varied crops.

sources.title: SOAS: The Legacies of Jean Boyd and Nana Asma’u Fodio
sources.note: SOAS archives 2022, reform movement and continuing educational legacy.

sources.title: Yves Person: Samori, chronology
sources.note: Scholarly chronology reproduced by web Mande; early 1860s rise, 1892 migration, 1896 to 1897 eastward state, capture 29 September 1898 and death 1900. One treaty date in transcription is inconsistent; not used.

sources.title: Martin Legassick: Firearms, Horses and Samorian Army Organization 1870 to 1898
sources.note: Journal of African History 7(1), 1966, 95 to 115; accessible extract and methodological caveat in note 2.

sources.title: UNESCO General History of Africa VII: African initiatives and resistance in West Africa
sources.note: Chapter on West African resistance, pp. 124 to 127: trade/arms, 1882 confrontation, 1885 Bure, treaties, strategic resistance.

sources.title: Gareth Austin: Cash Crops and Freedom (2009)
sources.note: Discussion of nineteenth-century growth of slavery, footnotes 25 to 26; Samori’s capture/sale of people to finance guns and horses.

sources.title: M’Brah Kouakou Désiré: Diawala, heir to Sordi (2019)
sources.note: Annales de l’Université de Moundou 6(1), 373 to 398; regional history based on archives, prior scholarship and oral traditions. Sordi is in northern Côte d’Ivoire, not Mali.

sources.title: David Robinson: The Holy War of Umar Tal, chapter 7
sources.note: Clarendon Press, 1985, chapter reproduced by webPulaaku. Segu campaign of 1859 to 1861, farming, river commerce, artisans and civilian suffering.

sources.title: BnF: Bibliothèque de Ségou authority record
sources.note: Collection begun by Umar from 1841 and inherited and enlarged by Ahmadu after 1864. Contains 518 volumes; at the BnF since 1892. Languages: Arabic and Fula.

sources.title: Review of the Inventory of the Umarian Library of Ségou (1986)
sources.note: Bulletin critique des Annales islamologiques 3, p. 136: library seized 1890, bound 1898 to 1901, international cataloging and microfilm.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Selections from the Treasure of Ahmadu
sources.note: Gold, silver and leather ornaments from the late eighteenth or early nineteenth century. Taken from earlier treasuries by Umar and from Ahmadu’s palace by France in 1890.

sources.title: Musée de l’Armée: Provenance research and restitutions
sources.note: Current institutional section on Senegal explicitly calls the sabre falsely attributed to El Hadj Omar; restitution authorized 2020.

sources.title: National Library of Tunisia: Umar al-Futi, Rimah (1876 edition)
sources.note: Catalog title: رماح حزب الرحيم على نحور حزب الرجيم. Author: Abu Hafs Umar al-Futi. Tunis state press, 1876, volume 1, 417 pages. This printed edition postdates the author.

sources.title: Biblissima/BnF: Amadou Tall
sources.note: BnF biographical authority: Umar’s son, ruler at Segu from 1864 to 1890. This does not mean all resistance ceased in 1890.

sources.title: Ahmet Kavas: Samori Ture, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi (2009)
sources.note: Scholarly encyclopedia biography, paragraphs on 1861 state formation, eastward migration, capture 29 September 1898 and death 2 June 1900. Other contested numbers and sweeping religious claims not adopted.

sources.title: Nana Asma’u, Admonition: scanned printed witness
sources.note: PDF page 1, printed page 21, first line: Arabic invocation before the Hausa Ajami verses. Undated printed witness, not an autograph. Image directly inspected during integration on 2026-09-21.
